provenance.notes: fresh GUI worker per cell, NEW empty foreground mesh, no background geometry; clicks, drags, panel typing, panel checkbox clicks and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Backspace are real input; no script call between the first click and the end of the stroke; stroke ended by the tool-drop key; mesh read once after it; history rows counted by a post-end walk of Ctrl+Z presses.

rig.view: top orthographic, 440 px per metre, points land on y = 1.0, click quantum 0.005 m
rig.flip_flag: the stroke's facing flag is decided at the 3rd point (see the facing fixture); A-points decide it ON, B-points OFF
rig.history_rows: rows = number of post-end Ctrl+Z presses that change the mesh; every cell below commits exactly ONE row (the first post-end undo empties the mesh, the second changes nothing)

law: While a stroke is live, Ctrl+Z restores the stroke to its state BEFORE THE LAST STROKE EVENT, one event per press, with nothing recorded in history. An event is anything that changed the stroke's state: a click adding a point, a drag of a point (the whole drag is one event), a typed panel value (each typed field is its own event, including the current-point index), and a panel checkbox write (the facing flag). The restored state includes the facing flag exactly as it was (no re-decision). Ctrl+Shift+Z re-applies the event just undone. Popping all points leaves the tool armed; the next clicks start a new stroke. Backspace is NOT handled by the stroke: it runs the editor's global delete, which is a no-op only when nothing is selected; with a selection it ends the stroke (committing it, the new element selected by the selectNew rule) and deletes the selection.
